tagline: Tandon School of Engineering · New York University
description: Cities extend their influence far beyond their physical boundaries, affecting ecosystems, climate, and societies worldwide. At the Urban Planet Lab, we study the dynamics and impacts of urbanization at multiple scales—from local neighborhoods to global systems—to better understand and address the complex challenges of our increasingly urbanized world.

cards.title: Cities as Complex Systems
cards.description: Cities and extreme weather are two complex dynamical systems that interact across scales, and urban heat is one of the many emergent outcomes. We bring systems thinking and tools such as fractals, scaling laws, and complex networks to understand how cities, their people and socio-economic systems, and the physical microclimate self-organize and impact each other.

cards.title: Multi-scale Urban Sensing
cards.description: Resilient cities need observation systems that resolve heat where people live, not only city-wide averages. We combine ground sensors, airborne instruments, and satellite-based remote sensing to characterize the urban form and fabric as well as heat across multiple spatio-temporal scales. This help us spot persistent hotspots, follow how heat evolves during extreme weather, and turn those observations into guidance for adaptation.

cards.title: Climate-conscious Urban Design
cards.description: We study how urban form, materials, and green infrastructure shape thermal landscape, and how socio-economic inequality, as well as historic social drivers such as redlining, determine today’s intra-urban heat disparities. Our work then aims to identify interventions such as cooling strategies, design choices, and targeted investments that would make cities more climate-resilient and equitable for all.
